headline: Lumentum's chief executive has warned that a shortage of the laser material indium phosphide could last longer than the shortage of memory chips for AI.
score_reason: Pool score 6 lowered by 2: the remarks are from 8 Jul 2026, about three months before this edition, and they are a company executive's own view relayed by one outlet.
importance_line: AI data centre builders could be slowed by a lack of laser parts that connect their chips, but the warning comes from a supplier of those parts and the article offers no independent check.
summary: Startup Fortune reports that Lumentum chief executive Michael Hurlston said at a conference in Paris on 8 Jul 2026 that the shortage of indium phosphide, the material used for the lasers in AI data centre network links, could become worse than the memory chip shortage. The article says Lumentum put demand for these lasers more than 30 percent above supply on its May earnings call, which could limit how fast data centres can connect their AI chips.
notes: The article does not state the year of the 8 July remarks; 2026 is inferred from context. Reader level: written at level five as the brief says; Full_Report rules 5.1 and the Drive phrasing file now list 7/10 for the Full Report (clash already with Rafi), level not changed.
